title: Terms of Payment: Due Dates, Late Payment Charges and Courtesy Waivers (Electric Service by Rate Schedule)
content:
These terms of payment govern every bill of an Electric Service by Rate Schedule account.

### 1. Due date

The due date of a bill is the bill date of the billing period's facility charge line plus the schedule's bill due days, in calendar days. The days are counted from the day after the bill date, the due date itself being the last day of the count.

### 2. When a late payment charge may be assessed

A late payment charge may be assessed only when the current date is later than the due date so counted. The authority is the system record of the facility charge line's bill date for that billing period on that service account. On the due date itself no late payment charge may be assessed; from the day after it, one may.

| Hypothetical Schedule R bill dated June 10 (20 bill due days) | Late payment charge may be assessed |
|---|---|
| June 30 (the due date, last day of the count) | No |
| July 1 (the day after the due date) | Yes |

### 3. Clauses no longer in force

The following former clauses of these terms are **no longer in force**; each is superseded by the current late payment charge basis of Electric Service by Rate Schedule:

- the clause defining the past-due amount of a bill as what remains of that bill after payments posted on or before the due date, payments being applied to the oldest unpaid charges first;
- the clause setting the charge as the schedule's late payment charge percentage of that past-due amount, rounded to the cent, never less than the schedule's minimum, assessed once per bill;
- the clause under which no late charge was assessed on a bill fully covered by an energy assistance pledge recorded on or before the due date, nor on the portion of a balance moved into an active payment arrangement;
- the clause stating that a late charge is never partly waived.

### 4. Courtesy waiver

A member may receive a courtesy waiver of one late payment charge. The waiver is posted as a bill credit with the reason late-charge waiver; its source is the late payment charge being waived and its amount equals that charge. A waiver is given only when both of the following hold:

- the number of late-charge waiver credits on the same service account dated in the 365 days ending on the day before the date of the waiver being considered is below the schedule's courtesy waivers per rolling 12 months; and
- the account has no returned payment posted within that same 365-day window.

| Waivers in the window (hypothetical Schedule R, allowance 1) | Returned payment in the window | Waiver may be given |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | None | Yes |
| 0 | One | No |
| 1 | None | No |

On Schedule LP, whose allowance is 0, no courtesy waiver can be given.

superseded_clauses: The past-due amount of the bill is what remains of that bill after payments posted on or before the due date, payments being applied to the oldest unpaid charges first.
The charge is late_charge_pct percent of that past-due amount, rounded to the cent, but never less than late_charge_minimum, and it is assessed once per bill.

No late charge is assessed on a bill whose past-due amount is fully covered by an energy assistance pledge recorded on or before the due date, nor on the portion of a balance moved into an active payment arrangement.
A late charge is never partly waived.
